headline: SoftBank is reportedly weighing a purchase of Allied Universal, America's biggest security services firm, as its founder Masayoshi Son looks to put AI-powered robots to work in more industries.
score_reason: Possible deal of up to $18 billion in equity (close to $30 billion with debt), carried by Bloomberg, Reuters and the Financial Times, but only at an early stage and from unnamed sources.
importance_line: It could affect the security guards at Allied Universal, whom Bloomberg's sources say SoftBank might in future replace in part with robots, and its backers Warburg Pincus and La Caisse, but the talks are early, nothing is agreed and humanoid security robots are said to need more time.
summary: Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter, that SoftBank Group, the Japanese technology investor, is considering buying Allied Universal in a deal that could value the privately held company at up to $18 billion in equity, or close to $30 billion counting about $12 billion of its publicly traded debt. The Financial Times' headline says the two sides are in talks, but Bloomberg, in Channel NewsAsia's summary, describes the discussions as early, with no decision yet on a deal or its price, and says SoftBank declined to comment.
notes: Source is Bloomberg; read at The Japan Times (carries Bloomberg's text, partly behind a subscription wall) plus Channel NewsAsia's summary via UA.NEWS. Bloomberg's own link was not available, so url is the Japan Times page. FT original (pool item) paywalled; its headline says 'in talks'.
